messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: p95 spike detected for Evergreen Financial (customer_id: ef-8421) on APSE1 dedicated pool. Current p95 latency = 2.1s (SLO 800ms). Error rate stable. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/respond. Autoscale attempts showing queue growth. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-isolation|tenant-isolation>

oncall-julia: ack. I'm on call. Paging @sarah-platform and @mike-sre. Can we confirm impact to customer SLA and whether this is tenant-local?
sarah-platform: looking at pool metrics now — I see one tenant (ef-8421-tenant-7) with sustained token throughput + concurrent sessions spike. Stack used: dedicate-gpu-a100-16. KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% in last 6m.
mike-sre: I'm seeing steady CPU/GPU saturations on nodes pinned to ef-8421. Other tenants in same pool show normal tail latency. Probably noisy-tenant behavior.
andrew-eng: if it's noisy-tenant, runbook says apply tenant-shield isolation (move offending tenant to isolated slice or throttle). Recommend quick isolation to protect others.
kelly-ops: @amanda-accounts can you confirm Evergreen is aware of potential degradation? We need to be clear about mitigation steps.
amanda-accounts: pinged evergreen cs lead, Jenna. She says they are seeing slow responses in production dashboards and open to a maintenance window if we need eviction.
incidents-bot: Runbook step 2: `assess-impact -> isolate-tenant`. To isolate: `rctl tenant isolate ef-8421-tenant-7 --pool apse1-dedicated --mode slice` (dry-run output below).
sarah-platform: running dry-run now.
```
$ rctl tenant isolate ef-8421-tenant-7 --pool apse1-dedicated --mode slice --dry-run
plan: create slice s-ef8421-iso-1 with 2gpus
plan: move 3 active sessions to slice simulator (no traffic cut)
plan: set qps-limit=20 for tenant while slicing completes
```

sarah-platform: dry-run looks good. Will apply with careful ramp. I'll push commands and watch p95 across pool.

oncall-julia: assign tasks: Sarah - isolation + monitoring, Mike - check autoscale / warm spare, Andrew - verify routing fallback, Kelly - customer comms.
mike-sre: warming spare nodes in ap-southeast2 warm pool and preparing cross-region route rule `route-policy: customer-warm-failover` (no DNS change; internal routing only). If slice move fails we can shift incoming traffic to warm pool for ef-8421 only.
sarah-platform: starting isolation now. Applying: `rctl tenant isolate ef-8421-tenant-7 --pool apse1-dedicated --mode slice --apply`
```
apply: provision slice s-ef8421-iso-1 -> 2xA100
apply: attach tenant ef-8421-tenant-7
apply: set qps-limit=20
status: move-in-progress (3 active sessions migrating)
```

sarah-platform: migration step 1 -> 2 complete. p95 pool (excluding slice) dropped from 2.1s -> 780ms. p95 for the tenant slice is currently 1.9s.
andrew-eng: good. That confirms noisy tenant. Next: consider persistent throttle or ask customer to optimize batch sizes. Could also evict long-running sessions if they block.
kelly-ops: Jenna (Evergreen) on call: "We can throttle for now, we'll investigate training job causing burst. Please notify when we move to failover." :thumbsup:
amanda-accounts: recording customer permission to throttle.
mike-sre: I'll trigger a temporary QPS cap at the routing layer while slice completes and warm pool is brought up. Command: `infractl route update --customer ef-8421 --qps 25`
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: route update succeeded. new qps cap=25 applied to ef-8421 across apse1 gateway instances.
incidents-bot: metric check: pool p95 now 760ms, pool p99 1.5s. Tenant slice p95 1.7s. Queue length decreasing.
oncall-julia: good containment. Next steps: keep slice and qps cap for 2 hours, follow-up with Evergreen on root cause. Create incident ticket and schedule postmortem.
sarah-platform: creating ticket INC-2026-8421 and linking relevant logs + graph snapshots.
```
Ticket: INC-2026-8421
Summary: Evergreen Financial - APSE1 p95 spike due to noisy tenant (ef-8421-tenant-7). Isolation applied; temporary qps cap and slice provisioned.
Attachments: /graphs/apse1/pool-ef8421-2026-03-15.png, /logs/ef8421/stream-1642.log
```

kelly-ops: I'll send a customer note: short note to Jenna summarizing actions + ETA for next update in 30m.
amanda-accounts: confirming. Jenna appreciates swift containment.
andrew-eng: recommend we set long-term limits in tenant onboarding to prevent runaway training jobs in dedicated pools. I'll open a follow-up RFC.
mike-sre: autoscale showed delayed provisioning because of quota fragmentation. We'll review autoscale tuning and warm capacity policies for dedicated pools.
oncall-julia: handing off to mitigation owner @sarah-platform for 1hr watch. If anything regresses, page again. Please add timeline and steps to the ticket.
sarah-platform: taking mitigation ownership. I'll post an update in 30m with metrics.
incidents-bot: :information_source: Incident status -> MITIGATED (containment achieved). Severity: SLO breach (customer-impact) -> mitigation in place. Postmortem required.
kelly-ops: documenting customer comms thread: "We isolated the noisy tenant and applied a temporary throttle. We're keeping you updated and will coordinate a longer maintenance window if needed."
amanda-accounts: noted. Jenna requested cc to security/compliance — will include.
incidents-bot: closing war room channel in 1h unless updated.
onduty-note: summary for postmortem: noisy tenant caused KV cache churn + heavy concurrent sessions. Isolation via slice + qps cap worked. Follow-ups: improve onboarding limits, autoscale warm policy, explore automated noisy-tenant detection.
